chunks: It was narrated from the Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) that he said:

You should say after the two evening prayers: 'O Allah, in Your hand are the destinies of the night and the day, the destinies of the world and the Hereafter, the destinies of death and life, the destinies of the sun and the moon, the destinies of victory and defeat, the destinies of wealth and poverty. O Allah, avert from me the evil of the wicked among the jinn and humans, and make my return to lasting goodness and enduring bliss.'

key_terms.الْعِشَاءَيْنِ: The two evening prayers (voluntary prayers performed after the obligatory Maghrib prayer)
key_terms.فَسَقَةِ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ: The wicked/transgressors among the jinn and humans
key_terms.مَقَادِيرُ: Destinies, measures, or decrees (plural of miqdar)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite after the two evening prayers according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this supplication is recited after the two voluntary evening prayers, serving as a concise affirmation of divine decree (*al-Qadar*) over both cosmic cycles and human destiny. It bridges theological concepts of God’s absolute control with practical spiritual needs, asking for deliverance from the evil of jinn and humans while seeking eternal bliss. This practice highlights the Shia emphasis on integrating daily devotional acts with remembrance of Allah’s power over life, death, and provision.
